title: Plan G: AI Coding Workflow (Requirements to Delivery)
summary: Clarify requirements → technical plan → scaffold → incremental coding → test & debug → review & commit
scenario: Best for new features, small tools, static sites and automation scripts — from a vague requirement to shippable code.

steps.title: Clarify requirements
steps.detail: Turn a vague requirement into clear acceptance criteria: goal, inputs/outputs, edge cases, and what NOT to build. Let the model ask the gaps you missed — this decides how much you rework.
steps.tips: Write 'when X happens, then Y' acceptance cases so the AI and you are on the same page.

steps.title: Technical plan
steps.detail: Decide stack and architecture (language, framework, data structures, interfaces) first, with the model comparing options and trade-offs. Settle the plan before writing code.
steps.tips: Ask for the simplest runnable MVP first, then expand — steadier than designing everything up front.

steps.title: Scaffold and skeleton
steps.detail: Initialize the project, directory structure, dependencies and base config until the code runs. Use templates or agent scaffolding to cut manual labor.
steps.tips: git init early and commit in small steps so anything can roll back.

steps.title: Incremental coding
steps.detail: Implement in small steps — finish one feature/module and verify it before moving on. Let coding agents (Claude Code / Cursor Composer) edit and run autonomously, so problems trace to a specific step.
steps.tips: Commit every verifiable unit; generating one giant feature at once is how big hidden bugs happen.

steps.title: Test and debug
steps.detail: Write unit tests for critical logic, manually verify edge and error paths, and feed error logs to the model for diagnosis. Let AI write tests, run them and fix regressions.
steps.tips: Describe exactly how to reproduce before asking the model — hit rate jumps; test empty, huge and invalid inputs separately.

steps.title: Review and commit
steps.detail: Self-review the diff, run an AI security/correctness/performance pass, fix findings, and write a clear PR description (what changed, why, how tested).
steps.tips: Include test results and reproduction steps in the PR; reviews pass faster and rollbacks are easy.

pitfalls.title: Coding before clarifying requirements
pitfalls.detail: Vague requirements mean guaranteed rework; ten minutes writing acceptance criteria is the cheapest investment.

pitfalls.title: Generating one giant feature at once
pitfalls.detail: Big one-shot output buries bugs where they're hard to find; incremental coding with per-step verification is the reliable rhythm.

pitfalls.title: Shipping without running tests
pitfalls.detail: AI code looks plausible but breaks at the edges; at minimum test the critical paths.

pitfalls.title: Stale libraries / guessed APIs
pitfalls.detail: Models may suggest outdated APIs; confirm library versions and signatures (e.g. with context7) or regenerate against current docs.
